attachments.origin_landmark: adjacent metacarpal shafts (each with 2 heads, bipennate)
attachments.insertion_landmark: extensor expansion + proximal phalanx base, digits 2 (both sides), 3, 4

actions: abduct fingers away from the axial line (digit 3); assist MCP flexion/IP extension

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: 4 separate small bipennate muscles (TA: interossei dorsales I-IV) modeled here as one collective entity; each originates from 2 adjacent metacarpal shafts, a genuinely bipennate architecture.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the dorsum of the hand, 1-2 cm proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints; or longitudinally along the palpable metacarpal shafts.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Four muscles lying between the metacarpal cortices I-V.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Spasticity here can subluxate the proximal phalanx anteriorly and flex the metacarpophalangeal joint past 90 degrees. A 2023 study supported the in-plane longitudinal dorsal approach as safe and effective.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

trigger_points.location_description: DI-1 (first dorsal interosseous): dorsal web palpation/needling against the second metacarpal, staying distal to the radial artery's passage between its two heads.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Has the widest map of the interossei: refers to the radial side of the index (strongest distally), deep into the dorsum and palm of the hand, with spillover that can reach the ulnar side of the hand and little finger.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Sustained pinch-grip against resistance (scissors, secateurs, chopsticks, dental and surgical instruments, climbing crimps, smartphones), writing pressure, post-fracture stiffness.
trigger_points.notes: Travell & Simons also observed an association between interosseous trigger points and Heberden's nodes at the DIP of the same ray -- recorded here as their clinical hypothesis, not established causation.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1, Ch. 40, pp. 786-793 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document

clinical.compiled_by: repository owner (physician); hand_intrinsic_muscles_reference_v1.html, compiled 03/09/2026. Source hierarchy used. (1) Peer-reviewed anatomical and biomechanical studies (bibliographic data and abstracts retrieved via PubMed/NCBI, 01–03/09/2026; DOIs linked in the reference list); (2) reference textbooks — Standring (Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., 2021), Kapandji (2007), Green's Operative Hand Surgery (8th ed., 2022), Brand & Hollister (1999); (3) Simons, Travell & Simons, The Trigger Point Manual Vol. 1, 2nd ed. (1999) and 3rd ed. (2019) for trigger-point (TrP) referral patterns; (4) StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf for cross-checking. No item below relies on blogs or unattributed aggregators; where secondary TrP summaries were used to confirm Travell & Simons figures, they are graded accordingly in the verification table.
clinical.function_biomechanics: Abduct the fingers from the third-ray axis, flex the MCPs, and extend the IP joints through the wing tendons — an IP-extensor effect that requires the MCP to be held out of hyperextension (the logic behind the Bouvier manoeuvre and anti-claw splinting/tendon rerouting) [3][21][31][35]. The interossei are the "foundation of hand function": they balance the extrinsic flexor–extensor tug-of-war at the MCP and set finger rotation for pinch [23]. DI-1 deserves its own sentence: PCSA in the extrinsic range [6], it rotates-supinates and braces the index against the thumb, and with AdP forms the pinch couple — key pinch collapses by ~77% under ulnar block [7]. Chronic imbalance in the other direction — intrinsic tightness/contracture after trauma, spasticity or RA — drives swan-neck posturing and participates in ulnar drift [35]. Morphological variants (accessory slips, extra heads) are common enough to matter in web-space surgery [10][39].
clinical.adjacent_structures: Relations · fascia · compartments: Between the metacarpals, dorsal to the DTML, each wrapped in its own osteofascial compartment (four of the ten hand compartments — release via two dorsal incisions) [4][35]; the dorsal interosseous fascia floors the dorsal subaponeurotic space; DI-1 shares the first web with AdP and is the one intrinsic you can inspect and palpate directly — its wasting is the earliest visible sign of ulnar neuropathy [1][3].

trigger_points.referred_pain: 40, pp. 786–793). Each dorsal interosseous refers pain primarily along the side of the finger to which it inserts, plus deep ache in the dorsum of the hand. DI-1 has the widest map: the radial side of the index (strongest distally), deep into the dorsum and palm of the hand, with a spillover that can reach the ulnar side of the hand and little finger [24][25]. Travell & Simons also observed an association between interosseous TrPs and Heberden's nodes at the DIP of the same ray — treat this as their clinical hypothesis, not established causation (verification row V22) [24].

pain_referred_into_this_muscle_from: Myofascial: extensor digitorum and extensor indicis (dorsal wrist→digit), ECRL/ECRB (dorso-radial), ECU (dorso-ulnar), coracobrachialis (posterior arm→dorsum), scalenes, subscapularis ("wrist-band"), latissimus (ulnar spill) [24].
Non-myofascial: radial sensory neuropathy, C7 root, extensor tenosynovitis/intersection syndromes, carpal boss, MCP synovitis [35].
clinical.pain_referred_into_territory: Pain referred TO the dorsum of the hand
clinical.caveat: Most myofascial hand pain is imported: shoulder-girdle, arm and forearm TrPs project distally far more often than intrinsic TrPs project proximally. Patterns below are the prototype maps of Simons, Travell & Simons (Vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1999; 3rd ed., 2019) — screening guides, not fingerprints; individual spread is wide [24][25]. Non-myofascial mimics are listed per zone for the same working position [5][29][31][35]. TrP → = habitual referred-pain direction of that muscle's trigger points (Simons, Travell & Simons 1999/2019); patterns are prototypes — individual variation is wide.
